name: John H Moss Lake Campground
evidence: City of Kings Mountain per-site sheet (cityofkm.com DocumentCenter/View/3401): sites 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 'Water view', 14-16 'Excellent water view'; the city's schematic (View/3398) draws a 28-site one-way loop east of the marina access road. NC911 2023 0.15 m orthophoto (Wayback 22252, z19): trailers on a gravel loop in pines just south of the dam's fenced spillway. USGS 3DEP profiles: north of the loop the ground rises to 759-764 ft (pool 734.4 ft) before the marina lot, but from the loop's NE corner (~750 ft) it falls into the spillway channel and open water starts ~110 m north - consistent with the views at 14-16, and the spillway between rules out on-water. Pin moved ~140 m from 35.2751,-81.4591 onto the loop (OSM camp node 35.27574,-81.45818); Campspot's pin 35.285271,-81.466865 is residential woods 1.3 km north.

name: Wild Nature Campground
evidence: Campspot (wildnaturecampground) sells 'Lake View Un-Serviced Site' (26, 27; 40 ft) and 'Electricity ONLY 15 AMP Lake View Site' (24, 25, 28-30; 30 ft); the operator's drone shot labels 24, 25 and 28-30 along the camp's south edge, and its 2021-09-17 photo from the 28/29 sign looks across open grass toward the water. Esri at 45.1000,-63.3875: those sites ring a sandy clearing ~55-70 m north of the tip of Lynch Lake (OSM way 84416981, ~120 x 100 m), reached by a track to a beach and dock with forest on both sides - a view down the opening, not a shoreline pad. Pin moved ~500 m east from the Hwy 2 entrance road (45.10126,-63.39400; Campspot's 45.10109,-63.392205 is the same road) onto the camp.

name: Arbuckle RV Resort
evidence: Campspot (arbucklervresort) sells 'Back In Lakeside' sites 12, 13, 16-20, 23, 24 and 26 (32-36 ft); its map draws one loop with ponds off the SW end. Esri at 34.4948,-97.0053: the south row's pads sit ~23-28 m from a shallow, partly drawn-down pond's high-water edge, across the camp's own gravel loop road and open grass, with trees only at the west end - the camp's own loop road is not a buffer (as 1565, 2115). The earlier reading cited a pond across the highway.

name: Epsom Valley Campground
evidence: Campspot (epsomvalleycampground) flags RV sites 05 (45 ft), 06 (32 ft), R-4 (40 ft) and R-5 (45 ft) 'Waterfront Site', sold as 'Live Free Waterfront' ('This wooded site sits right on the water'), and its per-site map draws them at the Suncook River's bank where the river bends around the camp. Esri (2024-10) and Wayback UC-G 2011-04-08 (0.3 m, leaf-off) are both canopy-blind under white pine, so the per-site flags and map govern (as 12635). Upgraded from riverview.

name: Green Park Provincial Park Campground
evidence: Campspot (KW Green Park RV Resort) sells '30Amp Water View two WAY RV Site' (101-114, 24, 26-34) and '30/50 Amp Waterview' (25, 55): 'Enjoy the view of the Trout River from your picnic table! The beach is only a short walk away.' The type's own photos (2023-07-18) show sites 30/31 and 32/33 on open lawn with the Trout River estuary in plain view, ~100 m off beyond a playground and picnic ground, nothing screening it; only cabins are sold as 'Beach Front'. Esri (2022-10, no RVs on site) shows the open shore fields. Not on-water (a used playground/picnic strip, and the distance), but open ground with the water unscreened is at least a view.

name: Sweet Minihaha Campground
evidence: Operator site map (sweetminihahacampground.com/map): loop A runs out to a BEACH on the Sugar River, sites 63-69 along it and 70-77 beside the road in; RoverPass sells 44, 45, 48, 49 and 70-74 as $60 'Preferred sites' (30 A + water, 27 ft) against $50 for the rest. Loop A is the river-wrapped peninsula at 42.6764,-89.4240, ~450 m west of the pin: Wayback UC-G 2011-04-29 (0.3 m, leaf-off) shows trailers parked on open grass ~10-25 m from the north bank, scattered trees only, and a sand beach at the tip; Esri 2021-07 shows the tip still open grass and sand to the water. The site's 'Waterfront - Along water edge' line is RoverPass's generic amenity checklist and wasn't used. The earlier reading looked from the County Road E entrance.

name: Black River Campsites
evidence: Re-checked 2026-10-14: RoverPass's park-level 'Waterfront' tick is the only claim (no per-site data or map). Esri (leaf-off) at 32.3466,-90.6650 and z19 at 32.3470,-90.6648: the camp clearing and the meadow sites south of it sit ~65-80 m from the Big Black River behind continuous bottomland forest, and the on-site pond (~70 x 50 m) is ~35 m east of the clearing through woods; no pad at either water. Default down.

name: High Island RV Park
evidence: Re-checked 2026-10-14: the operator's amenities and rates pages list 'Canal Spaces' (rate: CALL) without saying where they are. Esri at 29.5593,-94.3948 (250 m and 900 m frames): the park at 1921 4th St is a town block on High Island's salt dome; the marsh edge is ~300 m west and the nearest oilfield canal ~450 m, nothing at or in view of the park's 24 slabs. Not confirmable; default down.

name: Joseph Stewart County Park
evidence: Jackson County (jacksoncountyor.gov Joseph Stewart page): 'Some sites in B Loop have a lake view'; the county's campground map (StewartCampgroundMap.png, on OSIP imagery) puts B Loop at the west edge, nearest Lost Creek Lake. USGS 3DEP profile along 42.6842: the shore is 1,803 ft and the loop's bench 1,950-1,965 ft from ~115 m east, so B Loop looks down on the lake ~45 m above it across a wooded slope ~80 m wide (Esri at 42.6850,-122.6185) - a view, not access. CampLife's per-site data has no lake tags.

name: Del Mar Fairgrounds RV Park
evidence: Re-checked 2026-10-14: CampLife tags one space, 'Red Lot Space 1' ('Along river on fairgrounds facility'), 'Water-front'; the other 113 (Surf and Turf 64, Red Lot 50) carry no water tag, and neither CampLife nor the fairgrounds publishes a lot map. Esri (2026-01) over the whole fairgrounds: Surf & Turf (OSM 32.97744,-117.25508) is a gravel lot below the Hilton ~500 m from the river, and every fairgrounds lot is cut off from the San Dieguito River and lagoon by the coastal rail embankment and its scrub (west), Jimmy Durante Blvd (south-west) or a 75-100 m riparian band carrying the Coast to Crest trail (east overflow lot); the north edge is a drainage ditch along Via de la Valle. The Red Lot can't be placed; default down.

name: Woods-N-Waters Kampground
evidence: Re-audited 2026-10-14 (AWH #7): Campspot tags both of its full-hookup site types 'Waterfront Site', but the park's own Campspot site map (woodsnwaters_avail.json; map read 2026-10-14 for 2027-06-08) puts those sites (back-ins 003-006, 011, 012, 015, 018, 021; pull-throughs 013, 024, 025, 063, with 007 and 026 unmapped) in the inner loops, across the camp road and the clubhouse and playground from the fishing pond, so the tag belongs to the type, not to sites on the water. Esri satellite (z19, 0.23 m/px, leaf-off) at 39.1196,-85.9664: the RV lot nearest the pond sits behind a 10-15 m strip of trees on its north side, and no pad fronts the bank across open ground. Not waterfront.
